subrules.name: 702.197a
subrules.rule: Experience is a triggered ability. “Experience” means “Whenever this creature attacks, if it has two or fewer +1/+1 counters on it, put a +1/+1 counter on it.”

subrules.name: 702.197b
subrules.rule: If a creature with experience has three or more +1/+1 counters on it as the ability tries to resolve, it will have no effect.

subrules.name: 702.224a
subrules.rule: Decoy is a triggered ability that creates a delayed triggered ability. “Decoy” means “Whenever this creature attacks, create a tapped and attacking token that’s a copy of it, except it's a 1/1 Illusion instead of its other creature types.” and “Exile that token at the beginning of the next end step.”

subrules.name: 702.224b
subrules.rule: If a creature has multiple instances of decoy, each triggers separately.

subrules.name: 702.224c
subrules.rule: If a replacement effect causes the decoy ability to create multiple tokens, they will be exiled by the delayed trigger as well.

mechanics.original_reminder: Whenever this creature attacks, create a tapped and attacking 1/1 Illusion token that's a copy of it. Exile the token at the beginning of the next end step.
mechanics.executable_reminder: Whenever this creature attacks, create a tapped and attacking token that's a copy of this creature, except it's a 1/1 Illusion instead of its other creature types. Exile that token at the beginning of the next end step.

semantic_equivalence.evidence: Rule decoy specifies a copy with base power/toughness 1/1 and replacement creature subtype Illusion, preserving other types/colors/abilities; the delayed exile is next end step, including the source reminder variant incorrectly saying end of combat. Grant expansion binds this creature to the recipient.

subrules.name: 702.225a
subrules.rule: Rapture is a triggered ability. "Rapture" means "When this creature dies, return it to the battlefield with a haze counter on it. As long as it has a haze counter on it, it loses all abilities and can't block."

mechanics.original_reminder: When this creature dies, return it to the battlefield with a haze counter on it. It loses all abilities and can't block.
mechanics.executable_reminder: When this creature dies, return it to the battlefield with a haze counter on it. For as long as it has a haze counter on it, it loses all abilities and can't block.

semantic_equivalence.evidence: Rule rapture ties both ability removal and blocking restriction to the returned object retaining a haze counter; unlike the abbreviated source reminder, removing all haze counters ends both restrictions.
